case_study: Ireland — CRU Large Energy Users (Data Centre) Connection Policy CRU/2025236 + EirGrid Data Centre policy suite (May 2026)
theme: Jevons / rebound: per-unit efficiency gains in AI compute do NOT reduce total data-centre electricity demand; grid-level demand is driven by build-out volume, not per-query efficiency.

sources.org: Commission for Regulation of Utilities (CRU), Ireland
sources.title: The CRU Publishes its Decision on New Electricity Connection Policy for Data Centres
sources.supports: Data centres grew from 5% of national electricity demand in 2015 to 22% in 2024. EirGrid forecast: data centre electricity demand 9.4 TWh (2025) -> 14.6 TWh (2034); 22% of national demand (2024) -> 31% by 2034. Doubling relative to 2023 figures.

sources.org: Commission for Regulation of Utilities (CRU), Ireland
sources.title: CRU/2025236 Large Energy User connection policy decision paper
sources.supports: Total electricity demand grew 30% over past 10 years while data centre demand grew over 460%. Data centre share rose from circa 5% (2015) to circa 22% (2024). 2023->2024 data centre consumption grew 633 GWh = ~150,000 Irish households (avg 4,200 kWh/yr). Since 2015 data centre consumption grew 5,731 GWh = 1.36 million households. Market intelligence exercise: potential for 'in the order of 5.8GW additional demand capacity' for the data centre sector in Ireland in the medium term. Supersedes Direction CRU/21/124. 80% renewable electricity requirement with 6-year glide path. 10 MVA threshold for 100% MIC-matched dispatchable onsite/proximate generation or storage. Worked example: 30 MVA data centre needs 34.8 MW installed dispatchable generation (derating 0.863), 210 GWh/yr at 80% utilisation, 168 GWh renewable requirement, 54.9 MW onshore wind installed (35% CF), leaving 26.9 MW de-rated / 31.2 MW nameplate gas turbine.

sources.org: Commission for Regulation of Utilities (CRU), Ireland
sources.title: New Electricity Connection Policy for Data Centres (proposed decision)
sources.supports: Proposes onsite/local generation+storage matching requested data centre demand capacity; stepwise build-up; dispatchable participation in electricity market; annual renewable/emissions reporting by data centres to System Operators; constrained/unconstrained locational mapping. Electricity demand from data centres grew from 5% of national electricity demand in 2015 to 21% in 2023.

sources.title: Data Centre Constrained Area Overview
sources.supports: All-Ireland peak demand approximately 7.5 GW. Ireland has 2 GW of contracted data centres, mostly greater Dublin — nearly a third of entire Irish demand once fully connected. EirGrid Market Intelligence Exercise (requested by CRU, ref CRU/2025/04): continued interest in further 6 GW of data centre demand in Ireland; if all materialised it would DOUBLE the current system peak. Greater Dublin region considered fully constrained (short circuit levels). Shaping Our Electricity Future Roadmap V1.1 (2023): 300 MW additional data centre demand outside greater Dublin; EirGrid desktop assessment: 50-100 MW per site at Galway/Limerick/Cork 220 kV nodes, total 150-300 MW. c.20% increase in electricity demand over last ten years. Fault ride-through: data centres rapidly reducing demand causes whole-system frequency deviation; 'The oscillating demand characteristics of Artificial Intelligence data centres could also pose a risk to the stability of the Irish system.'

sources.title: Data Centre Connection Offer Process and Policy, Version 3 (DCCOPP V3, IOO-CC-001-R3)
sources.supports: Implements CRU/2025236 for all new data centre connection applications >=1 MVA received on or after 2025-12-12. Data centre with MIC >= 10 MVA must provide dispatchable onsite/proximate generation or storage equal to 100% of MIC (derated). 80% renewable requirement assessed in Year 7 (6-year glide path); failure to meet allows EirGrid to reduce MIC or terminate the Connection Agreement. A data centre application CANNOT progress if it is in a constrained area. 30 MVA example requires ~34.8 MW dispatchable generation. EirGrid requires up to 18 calendar months to process Nominated Generation applications.
